title: Keyboard-first resize preview and persisted density presets for virtual tables
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table currently supports pointer-driven column resizing and density toggles, but keyboard interactions are inconsistent, there is no live-width preview during drag or keyboard adjustments, and team-level density preferences are not persisted. This causes accessibility gaps for keyboard-only users and a poor discoverability of density presets for power users.

Scope: Design patterns, interaction specs, and visual assets for: (1) keyboard-first column resizing with a live preview overlay, (2) a committed/cancel flow for resize via keyboard and pointer, (3) persisted density presets (collapsed/compact/comfortable) per workspace and per user, and (4) interaction rules with virtualization (eg. reflow, measurement, and scroll preservation). We will produce Figma components, an updated tokens list for density spacing, and an accessibility checklist for engineering.

Goals:
- Provide fully keyboard-operable column resize (start/stop/cancel, step granularity).
- Surface a transient live preview showing target column width and resultant layout impact before commit.
- Save density presets to user preferences and expose a quick toggle in the table toolbar.
- Ensure behavior is robust with virtualization (no layout jumps, minimal reflows).
- Meet WCAG keyboard and focus-visible expectations and include automated a11y tests.

Out of scope: UI for column grouping or advanced drag-and-drop column reorder (separate work item).
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard flow: focus on column resizer (via Tab), press Enter or Space to start resizing mode, use ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to change width in 8px steps, PageUp/PageDown to change in 32px steps, Enter to commit, Esc to cancel back to original width.
Pointer flow: drag shows same live preview overlay; release commits, Esc (while dragging) cancels and snaps back.

Preview overlay: shows numeric width in pixels, column label, and a subtle ghost outline of affected columns; overlay should be non-interfering for screen readers (aria-hidden) while controls are active.

Density presets: three presets (Compact, Regular, Comfortable) that change row height, vertical paddings via design tokens; presets persist per-user and per-workspace and are surfaced in table toolbar and table settings modal.

Virtualization compatibility: when resizing committed, virtualization layer remeasures only affected columns and preserves scroll position; while live preview is active, virtualization continues rendering without expensive reinitialization (use measurement cache).

Accessibility: keyboard focus is always visible and announced via SR to indicate resize mode; all resize actions exposed to screen readers via live region announcements (e.g., "Column 'Name' resized to 160 pixels").
Documentation: Figma components, interaction spec, ARIA attributes list, and engineering checklist published in the Design System repo and linked in this ticket.
design_notes: Introduce a lightweight 'resize preview' overlay component that attaches to the resizer handle and draws a ghost column width preview across the table canvas.
Use 8px base step derived from spacing token (grid-unit) and provide modifier steps for PageUp/PageDown. Allow a user-controlled finer granularity only when Alt/Option is held (4px).
Persist density preset as a key in the Design System user preferences store; expose API for Console to read/write so Dedicated/Private deployments can respect org defaults.
Focus state: when entering keyboard resize mode, set a modal-like input trap on the resizer (but keep the rest of the table interactive for pointer events) and announce the mode via SR-live region.
Visual language: preview is semi-opaque with 2px dashed outline and subtle shadow; numeric label uses token 'type-xs-semibold' and tokenized color 'fg-on-surface-contrast'.
Testing: provide a11y QA scenarios and component unit snapshots for both pointer and keyboard flows; include visual regression tests for presets.
tradeoffs: Live preview requires additional measurement reads which can affect performance; mitigate by debouncing preview updates and using cached column measurements maintained by the virtualization layer.
Persisting presets per-user increases storage surface (preferences) and sync complexity across devices; choose lightweight keys and default to workspace-level setting when user value is absent.
Full 'undo' history for resizes is out-of-scope; we provide immediate cancel via Esc and recommend telemetry for later additions.
